explanation: Chillies, native to the Americas, reached India after 1500 on European ships. Romans had imported Indian black pepper some 1,500 years earlier. Before chillies, Indian cooks got heat from pepper and ginger.

claims.text: Black pepper imported from India was widely used in Roman cooking by the 1st century AD.
Chilli peppers, native to the Americas, reached India only after 1500, carried by European traders.
Before chillies arrived, Indian cooking got its heat from black pepper, ginger and other seasonings.

issues.note: 'Indians cooking with chillies' has a second reading: Indigenous peoples of the Americas, long called Indians, cooked with chillies thousands of years before Roman pepper, which flips the answer. Relabel as 'Cooks in India using chillies' or 'People in India cooking with chillies'.

editor.reason: B revise: the label Indians cooking with chillies can be read as Indigenous Americans, who cooked with chillies long before Roman pepper, which flips the answer (§3.2). Relabelling changes a claim-bearing label, and c1 has no countable external evidence (A's calls count at Tier C or give no date), so a tiebreak cannot save it as written. Cut.
